_README: Co-change couplings: 'if you touched X this turn, you should also have touched one of Y'. Read by jit-memory.py (PreToolUse: surfaces the rule BEFORE the write) and enforce-cochange.py (Stop: catches the omission at end of turn). Data, not code: adding a coupling is a data edit, no hook change needed.
_WHY: Most rules you write down are recall-dependent: they only fire if the assistant thinks to consult them at the moment of acting, and that is exactly when it doesn't. A coupling turns 'remember to also do Y' into something checked every time. The ones below ship as examples that protect the harness itself; replace or extend them with your own.
_SEMANTICS: A coupling fires when at least one `when_touched` glob matched a file written this turn AND no `requires_one_of` glob did. `requires_one_of` is deliberately generous: the point is to catch 'you did none of these', not to police which one. Globs match forward-slashed absolute paths, case-insensitively; `**/` matches any depth. Each coupling is surfaced at most once per session per hook.
_HOW_TO_ADD_YOUR_OWN: Copy an entry, give it a unique `id`, list the files that trigger it in `when_touched`, the files that satisfy it in `requires_one_of`, a one-sentence `reason` the assistant will read, and a `rule` pointer (a memory file, rule file or doc that explains it). See _EXAMPLES for shapes that fit common vaults. If a coupling fires where the omission was legitimate, narrow its globs; do not switch the hooks off.

_EXAMPLES.reason: A decision record changed but the decision log did not. Readers find decisions through the log.
A report changed with no change to the notes it cites. Numbers in a report need a traceable source.

couplings.reason: A hook or its wiring changed with nothing written down about it. Hooks are the least discoverable part of the harness: undocumented, a hook is behaviour nobody can predict or audit.
A command, agent or workflow changed but the capability catalogue did not. If it isn't in CAPABILITIES.md, nobody knows it exists or what it does.

docs/*.html is generated from site/pages/ by site/build.mjs, so an edit to the published copy is overwritten by the next build. Edit site/pages/ and rebuild. (docs/index.html is the exception: it is standalone.)
